subject: Telemetry ingress gateway for private deploy — acceptance & test window
messages:

Subject: Observability ingress for our VPC/private deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team has a few follow-ups before we sign off on the private deployment: we need a short acceptance test runbook showing how telemetry (logs/metrics/traces) leaves our VPC, what TLS/mTLS boundaries look like, and exactly what evidence we can pull into our SIEM (Splunk).

Key asks:
- Describe the ingress gateway that will accept telemetry from the Redwood private control-plane and the customer-side forwarder (syslog/HEC).
- Firewall and egress rules required (ports, hosts).
- Sample Splunk HEC config and expected fields / event mapping.
- How trace context headers are preserved for cross-service correlation.
- Proof-of-acceptance check steps and sample artifacts we can upload to our PCI audit folder.

Can your team produce a short runbook and a 2-hour test slot next week? Prefer Thu 7/22 10:00-12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Samir
Acme Corp — Security Engineering

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. I'm proposing we own the runbook and lead the test. High level plan below; please review and flag gaps.

Plan (short):
1) Build an "ingress gateway" runbook that documents: expected customer forwarder behavior, auth (mTLS to our ingress proxy), permitted egress destinations (Splunk HEC IPs / FQDNs or customer-hosted collector), and trace propagation headers (traceparent / baggage).
2) Provide Splunk HEC example payload and a small mapping script for their SIEM team.
3) Acceptance checklist (we'll capture: connection handshake screenshots, Splunk index events, a short pcap of TLS handshake if needed, and a signed attestation doc).
4) Test window Thu 7/22 10:00-12:00 PT; validate with Acme and Splunk onboarding.

Jonas/Tessa: can you draft the runbook + checklist? Ben/Marissa: I need the HEC config snippet and a replay script to push sample events during test.

I'll coordinate with Acme for scheduling.

-kim

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Observability ingress for our VPC/private deployment

Kim / team,

Draft runbook attached (obsv_ingress_gateway_runbook_v1.pdf) and a concise acceptance checklist (obsv_acceptance_checklist.xlsx). Highlights and deviations from our hosted flow:

- Ingress model: we run an ingress proxy in the customer's VPC enclave that terminates customer mTLS for forwarder agents (syslog-ng, fluentd). That proxy then forwards to a hardened egress tunnel into Redwood's private egress gateway using mutual-auth and a dedicated TLS profile.
- Auth: customer <-> ingress-proxy: mTLS (client cert issued by customer or Redwood CA per contract). ingress-proxy <-> redwood-egress: mTLS with cert rotation via KMS.
- Ports: inbound 6514 (TLS syslog), 443 (HEC), and 9411 for Zipkin/collector HTTP traces (optional). Outbound from the enclave to Redwood egress: 443 only (destination FQDNs pinned in firewall rules).
- Trace propagation: we preserve W3C traceparent and baggage. For older instrumentation we map X-B3 headers. Our proxy injects a redwood_trace_id header for internal correlation.
- SIEM mapping: provided splunk_hec_config_snippet.txt in attachment. Key fields we guarantee: service.name, env, redwood_instance_id, original_host, syslog_program, timestamp_ns, trace_id.

Acceptance artifacts:
- Successful mTLS handshake (proxy logs + cert fingerprint)
- Splunk event with the sample event_id (event_id=redwood-acme-test-<timestamp>)
- Trace span showing end-to-end trace including downstream service call
- Signed attestation PDF produced by Redwood after validation

Open questions for Acme: do you require egress to go to your Splunk instance directly, or would you rather Redwood forward to Splunk cloud on your behalf? The runbook covers both paths.

-Jonas

Attachment: obsv_ingress_gateway_runbook_v1.pdf
Attachment: obsv_acceptance_checklist.xlsx
Attachment: splunk_hec_config_snippet.txt

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <sec-acct@acme.com>, Splunk Onboarding <onboard@splunk.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T16:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Observability ingress for our VPC/private deployment

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications before the test:

1) For mTLS do you support customer-managed certs that chain to our internal PKI, or must we use Redwood's CA? We prefer customer-managed for audit traceability.
2) On the Splunk mapping: can you include a small example of a syslog message converted to HEC payload so our Splunk admin can validate field extraction?
3) We want the test to demonstrate tracecontext continuity from a synthetic request coming from our service through Redwood and back. Is the replay script going to generate a full trace?

Thu 7/22 10:00-12:00 PT works for us. Could we schedule a 15-minute prep call 30 minutes before the window to validate certs?

Regards,
Samir

P.S. Splunk onboarding will join the test to receive HEC traffic; cc'd them here.

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.com>, Splunk Onboarding <onboard@splunk.com>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability ingress for our VPC/private deployment — test plan confirmed

Samir — all good. Quick answers and final plan: 

1) Customer-managed certs: supported. We'll accept a cert chain from your internal PKI; our ingress-proxy supports customer client certs and CRL/OCSP checks. We'll document the CSR/key steps in the runbook.
2) Splunk example: Ben attached a sample conversion (splunk_hec_config_snippet.txt) and we'll paste a syslog -> HEC example during the prep call.
3) Replay script: yes — the script will generate a synthetic trace with service A -> B -> C calls and propagate W3C traceparent headers. We'll capture a trace in our APM and show the event in Splunk.

Prep call: Thu 7/22 09:30 PT (15m) to verify certs and firewall rules. Test window: 10:00-12:00 PT. Please share the pre-provisioned cert bundle and the IP ranges you will open (we will provide the Redwood egress FQDN/IPs in the runbook).

Next steps: Jonas will update the runbook with CSR details; Ben will add the syslog->HEC payload example; I will create the attestation template and calendar invites.

Thanks all — looking forward to the run.

-kim

Attachments: obsv_ingress_gateway_runbook_v1.pdf; obsv_acceptance_checklist.xlsx; splunk_hec_config_snippet.txt
